phases.title: This Week
phases.blurb: Foundational moves. Don't start Phase 2 until these four are done. The way you spend Sunday afternoon and Tuesday night this week sets the trajectory.

phases.title: Before Summer
phases.blurb: Short-term priorities. PPP conversations, vision-statement workshop, Dinner with a Purpose, and the Easter goal of every soul reassessed.

phases.title: Ongoing Rhythms
phases.blurb: These never end. They become the heartbeat of AAC: the discipleship questions before financials, the vision said every Sunday, the testimony in every sermon.

phases.title: Summer
phases.blurb: Deploy the mission outward. Farmers Market, ace pairings, Easter benchmarking. The summer is when we test whether the formation became reproduction.

actions.title: Restructure the elder meeting agenda
actions.body: Move attendance & financials to the end. Open every meeting with: (1) Who is in a relationship with someone who doesn't know Jesus? (2) Who came to faith or took a major step this month? (3) Who moved stages in the pipeline?

actions.title: Name your 3–5 evangelism aces
actions.body: The people who naturally and comfortably share their faith. Write their names down. These people will lead the sniper pairing model.

actions.title: Begin drafting a new vision statement
actions.body: Dynamic, simple, includes next-generation and Ashe County specificity. Draft candidate: "Ashe Alliance exists to make and multiply disciples of every generation in Ashe County and beyond."

actions.title: Form the 5-person PPP team
actions.body: Nate + Jordan + at least 2 women + 1 elder. Assign each of the people in the dashboard to a specific team member for a PPP conversation.

actions.title: Run weekly PPP conversations
actions.body: Every team member takes one person to coffee or a meal each week. Ask: What are you passionate about? What breaks your heart? What are you naturally gifted at? Update the dashboard after each conversation.

actions.title: Include an evangelism story in every Sunday sermon
actions.body: Even if it didn't result in a conversion. "I am so proud of Bill for taking that leap." What is rewarded is repeated.

actions.title: Host a "Dinner with a Purpose"
actions.body: Volunteer appreciation night with a free meal, games, and prizes — that's the draw. Have key leaders personally call the fringe 50. Include 10–15 minutes of vision casting embedded in gratitude.

actions.title: Apply Notice / Compliment / Invite for children's wing
actions.body: Stand near nursery check-in. Find calm, well-adjusted families. Compliment their parenting. Ask for a 20-minute once-a-month commitment — not changing diapers, just telling a story.

actions.title: Workshop the revised vision statement
actions.body: Test it: Is it dynamic (expresses movement)? Simple (7 words or fewer)? Compelling (does it make people want to join)? Finalize and begin saying it every Sunday.

actions.title: Preach a 4-week series on the Great Commission
actions.body: Don't announce a new direction — create a "crisis of understanding" where the congregation grasps the gap between where AAC is and where God is calling it. Let them arrive at the vision themselves.

actions.title: Multi-church youth event (end of April)
actions.body: Already in planning. Execute well. Early test of the community engagement model. Have your aces present and intentional in conversations.

actions.title: Easter target: 100% PPP completion
actions.body: Every person in the dashboard should have had a PPP conversation and an updated, honest stage assignment. The dashboard should show real distribution across all five pipeline stages.

actions.title: Open every elder meeting with the 3 discipleship questions
actions.body: Before any numbers. Review the Shepherding dashboard together. Celebrate every person who moved a stage. Track Multiplying as the long-term church health indicator.

actions.title: Say the vision statement every Sunday
actions.body: In announcements, during giving, or at the opening. Jim's rule: "By the time you're tired of saying it, people are just starting to get it."

actions.title: Embed evangelism stories in every sermon
actions.body: At least one story of a congregation member living on mission — sharing their faith, serving a neighbor, discipling someone. Evangelism culture is built through narrative, not announcements.

actions.title: Record video testimonies
actions.body: 5-minute smartphone testimonies of evangelism experiences. Play them during the service. Production time: under 30 minutes. Let the church see that ordinary people share their faith.

actions.title: Quarterly: update the pipeline snapshot
actions.body: Real numbers from the dashboard. Compare against goals. Adjust strategy. The metrics that get tracked are the metrics that grow.

actions.title: Use Stage Transition Pathways pastorally
actions.body: When someone is stuck at a stage, ask — what's the specific next step for this person? PPP conversation → Serve team → Sniper pairing → Timothy assignment.

actions.title: Research Ashe County cultural centers
actions.body: Where do people already congregate with strangers? Farmers Market is identified. Find 2–3 others: schools, seasonal events, community gatherings.

actions.title: Lock in Farmers Market presence for summer
actions.body: Don't just set up a table — make the event better. Create a reason to linger. Wear matching shirts. Have your aces present and working the crowd naturally.

actions.title: Pair aces with rookies for outreach
actions.body: At least one outreach event before summer ends. Debrief afterwards. Ask: What happened? What felt natural? Who do you want to follow up with?

actions.title: Use Easter as growth benchmark
actions.body: Last Easter's attendance is this year's average attendance goal. Identify what barriers showed up (parking, children's space, seating) — fix them before next Easter.

actions.title: Consider one service for summer
actions.body: Wave-surfing strategy. Full room, rested volunteers, easier to build community. Re-evaluate two services in the fall as attendance climbs past 100.
